purpose: Defines the physical/institutional research-capacity model used by the Adaptive Research System.

effective_lab_unit.name: Effective Research Lab
effective_lab_unit.description: A normalized research-capacity unit. Early facilities commonly equal one effective lab. Later institutes, orbital complexes, biological research organisms, machine-science arrays, alien facilities, or other species-specific equivalents may contribute multiple effective units while remaining aggregate simulation objects.
effective_lab_unit.note: 400 RP/year is the early playable balance value and remains subject to later campaign tuning.

directed_program_model.description: A directed program is a major research project explicitly selected by the player or AI. Civilizations still conduct diffuse scientific work outside directed programs.

early_game.reason: Keeps the 2050-era research interface simple and represents limited strategic coordination of major civilization-scale research programs rather than claiming all scientists research one subject.
early_game.unallocated_capacity: Produces basic-science progress, field competence, hypotheses, evidence processing, and low-intensity exploratory work.

progression.description: Starting capability. The government/player can formally concentrate on one major strategic program at a time.
Research-network institutions let independent institutes sustain two major coordinated programs without collapsing administrative efficiency.
Multiworld scientific administration can coordinate several strategic research portfolios simultaneously.
There is no arbitrary project-slot ceiling. Each active program must still meet its own minimum allocated-lab requirement, so physical scientific capacity remains the constraint.

project_lab_requirements.description: Every directed project has a minimum effective-lab requirement. A project cannot start until that amount can be exclusively assigned.

allocation_example.result: Both projects can run simultaneously because the civilization supports two directed programs and has enough lab capacity to satisfy both allocations.

lab_scaling.description: Assigning more than the minimum accelerates research, but large programs have diminishing returns because coordination, duplicated experiments, and specialist bottlenecks increase.

research_pressure_gate.description: Pressure represents recognized need/evidence rather than scientific labor. It is not spent. A technology is pressure-gated only when its requirements explicitly declare required_pressure or required_pressure_any.

example.behavior: Before pressure reaches 25 the branch may remain unknown or merely hypothesized. At/above 25, assuming knowledge prerequisites are satisfied, it can appear as an investigable project. It still cannot be started until two effective labs can be assigned.

research_points.description: RP determines project progress after a project becomes available and receives enough labs.
research_points.reason: A civilization should not bank centuries of generic RP and instantly finish a newly discovered branch. Scientific capacity exists in active institutions and accumulated field competence, not a magical universal currency vault.

player_ui_progression.hidden_information_rule: Do not show pressure meters for undiscovered fields in a way that reveals hidden future technologies.

performance_rule.description: Late-game research capacity is stored as aggregate effective-lab capacity by relevant institution/region/field. Thousands of physical laboratories do not require thousands of active simulation objects.
